01 / Platform

Your project information, connected.

Instead of hunting through scattered spreadsheets, email threads and disconnected systems, the platform concept brings each project into one understandable view.

Why it matters Everyone works with clearer context, using the systems they already know.

01

Link commercial and engineering data

Bring order status from ERPNext together with drawing references from Tekla and fabrication information from PowerFab.

02

Understand every handoff

See which team holds the next action, what has been approved and where a revision may matter.

03

Keep existing tools

The proposed intelligence layer reads and interprets information; it does not replace source systems of record.

INTERACTIVE EXAMPLE

Explore the connected systems

Interactive concept using sample sources, not an active integration.

02 / Operations

Know where every project stands.

Customers and managers should not need five separate calls to understand progress. A connected operations view is intended to show project stages, owner assignments, blockers and delivery readiness.

Why it matters Identify delays early and coordinate the right response.

01

Project status in one place

Understand approvals, procurement, manufacturing, dispatch and installation readiness.

02

Blockers with ownership

Surface pending decisions or handoffs together with the responsible team.

03

Useful reporting

Provide clear progress summaries without confusing estimates with verified completion.

INTERACTIVE EXAMPLE

Explore an example operations dashboard

Illustrative project and machine metrics only. No live project connection.

03 / Machines

Understand the factory floor.

Where supported by machine controllers, connected production signals could help teams see machine availability, downtime and output, instead of relying only on manual updates.

Why it matters Improve visibility of machine performance and potential disruption.

01

Machine status

Capture operating or stopped signals where approved PLC and gateway access exists.

02

Downtime context

Relate relevant alerts to production schedules so teams can investigate faster.

03

Production insight

Summarize selected cycle counts, output and quality signals when instrumentation supports them.

INTERACTIVE EXAMPLE

Explore sample factory signals

Simulated telemetry, not data from connected machinery.

04 / AI Copilot

Ask a question. Find the source.

Imagine asking what is holding up a delivery, who owns a pending drawing or what changed in production. The proposed AI Copilot aims to return a grounded answer with its evidence.

Why it matters Reduce the time spent chasing updates and assembling reports.

01

Natural language questions

Ask about projects, engineering changes, procurement or delivery status.

02

Evidence before conclusions

Show relevant source documents, timestamps and limitations with an answer.

03

Human decisions stay in control

Any write action should require the right permissions and explicit confirmation.

INTERACTIVE EXAMPLE

Try a sample AI Copilot conversation

Sample questions and responses only. No access to live company records.

05 / Architecture

Built around enterprise controls.

Useful intelligence depends on trust. The proposed architecture keeps existing enterprise systems authoritative and designs for role-based access, auditability and controlled factory integration.

Why it matters Connect information without making operations or sensitive data openly accessible.

01

Access by responsibility

Design permissions around what a sales, engineering, production or management user actually needs.

02

Traceable information

Associate summaries and AI-assisted answers with their original systems and document references.

03

Conservative machine access

Plan secure edge connections with appropriate OT network isolation and review before deployment.

INTERACTIVE EXAMPLE

Explore the access-control concept

Demonstration of proposed permissions; not proof of a deployed security configuration.

06 / Roadmap

Where connected operations could go next.

The longer-term vision extends beyond reporting, with carefully validated AI and automation for scheduling, risk detection, quality and maintenance.

Why it matters A transparent view of planned directions, not promises of currently available features.

01

Production planning

Investigate dynamic scheduling that accounts for production constraints and changes.

02

Quality and maintenance

Explore computer vision inspection and predictive machine-health approaches.

03

Digital twins and workflows

Study connected asset models and human-approved automation across project processes.

Future concepts are subject to research, engineering validation and separate rollout decisions.
